plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Probability, Years 5 and 6 (VC2M5P02, VC2M6P02): conduct repeated chance experiments, record results and use frequency to describe outcomes
plan.shape: example-first with a live coin experiment in the launch, so relative frequency is built from data the class just made
plan.criticalFeature: relative frequency = the times it happened out of the total number of trials
decisionPoints: the choice check: 12 heads in 20 tosses
the hinge: relative frequency of yellow as a percentage
plan.anchor: chance = the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Show one equal spinner and write P(red) as parts we want out of all the parts before the launch.

manipulatives: A demonstration coin for the launch
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: chance = the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes
A blank tally chart for 10 coin tosses: heads, tails

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Run a coin experiment, convert relative frequencies, read dice results, fix a mistake and reason about small samples.
resources.title: Chance Experiments
resources.subtitle: Relative frequency = times it happened out of the total trials.

example.prompt: 4 heads in 10 tosses. What is the relative frequency of heads?

items.prompt: Toss a coin 20 times with a partner. Tally each toss, then fill in the table.

example.prompt: 8 reds in 20 spins. Write the relative frequency three ways.

items.prompt: Write each relative frequency as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage.

example.prompt: A dice was rolled 30 times. 3 came up 5 times. Relative frequency of 3?

items.prompt: Zoe spun a spinner 20 times. Red came up 8 times. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.answer: The bottom number is all the trials: 8/20 = 2/5 = 40%.

items.prompt: Tom tossed a coin 10 times and got 7 heads. Is the coin unfair?
items.explain: 10 tosses is a small number of trials, so results can be far from half. Toss it many more times before deciding.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Combining class results, two-dice totals and planning your own experiment, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Bigger Experiments
resources.subtitle: Combine results. List every outcome.

example.prompt: Group A: 6 heads in 10. Group B: 4 heads in 10. Combined?

items.prompt: Group A: 13 heads in 20 tosses. Group B: 8 heads in 20 tosses. What is the combined relative frequency of heads, as a percentage?
Why is the combined result closer to 50% than either group on its own?
items.answer: More trials: 40 tosses give a better picture than 20, so the result settles closer to the expected half.

example.prompt: How many ways can two dice total 3?

items.prompt: Two dice are rolled and added. Fill in the totals table, then answer below.
Which total is most likely? What is its probability?

example.prompt: Plan an experiment for a bag of 3 red and 1 blue counter.
steps: Pick, record, put it back, 20 times.

items.prompt: Plan an experiment with a bag of counters you choose. Write your prediction as a fraction, how many trials you will do, and how you will record the results.
items.answer: Check: a stated bag, a predicted probability, a number of trials (more is better), replacing the counter each time, and a tally table.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: totals of 10 and 100, a fraction frame, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Relative Frequency: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Times it happened out of the total trials.

items.hint: Each toss out of 10 is worth 10%.

items.prompt: 52 heads in 100 tosses. Write it as a percentage.
17 sixes in 100 rolls. Write it as a percentage.

slides.notes: Session 2 of our probability week: today we run chance experiments and describe what happened.

Before you start, put boards, markers and a coin per pair on desks, and draw a blank tally chart on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Read the scale
prompts: The scale starts at 50. Shop A sold 54, Shop B sold 58. How many more did B sell?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's graphs.
ASK: How many more did Shop B sell than Shop A?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> point to the bottom of the scale, 50, then read both values. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 58 take away 54 is 4. The scale starts at 50,
so the columns exaggerate it. Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying 'about double'.
Fix: read both values from the scale, and they subtract.
notes.prep: Review of Week 3 statistics (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: Which quadrant is 4, negative 2 in?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: the fourth
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> say right or left, then up or down, together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's the fourth quadrant: right 4 and down 2. Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying the second.
Fix: ask whether negative 2 is up or down, and they rename it.

beats: ASK: How do you write seven twentieths as a percentage?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 35%
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> make the denominator 100: times top and bottom by 5. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 7 twentieths is 35 hundredths, which is 35 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 7% or 72%.
Fix: multiply top and bottom by 5 to get hundredths, and they rewrite it.

beats: SAY: Now for our seven times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 7 times 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 63
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 7 tens is 70, take one 7 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 63. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 56 or 72.
Fix: use 7 tens is 70, take away 7, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's a bigger one.
ASK: What is 7 times 12?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 84
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 7 tens plus 7 twos. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 84. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 74.
Fix: 7 tens is 70 and 7 twos is 14,
add them, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many sevens make 42?
ASK: What is 42 divided by 7?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 6
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in sevens to 42. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 6. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 7.
Fix: check: 7 sevens is 49, too many, so it's 6, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to run a chance experiment and describe the results as a fraction, decimal and percentage.
successCriteria: I can record the results of a chance experiment in a frequency table.
I can write a relative frequency as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage.
I can explain what the relative frequency tells me about the chance.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we worked out the chance of something happening.
Today we test it by running real experiments.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 recording results is reachable for everyone; SC2 relative frequency three ways is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 interpreting it is the stretch.

slides.title: Toss a coin 10 times
slides.prompt: Predict: how many heads in 10 tosses?

beats: SHOW the coin.
SAY: I'm going to toss this coin 10 times,
and we'll tally every toss on the board.
ASK: Before I start, how many heads do you predict in 10 tosses?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 5. ACCEPT: 4 to 6
MODEL tossing 10 times, tallying each on the board.
SAY: Let's count them together as I tally: heads or tails?
SAY: We predicted about 5, and our result is what it is.
Today we'll describe results like ours as a fraction, a decimal and a percentage.
trap: expecting exactly 5 every time.
Fix: say results vary, and they compare with a neighbour's toss later.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: live data for the I Do. Keep the board tally for later. Under 5 minutes.

slides.meaning: How often an outcome happened, out of all the trials.
slides.example: 3 heads in 10 tosses is a relative frequency of 3/10.

notes.answer: times it happened out of all trials
beats: POINT to the words.
SAY: These words are relative frequency. Say them with me: rel-a-tive fre-quen-cy.
SAY: Frequency is how many times it happened.
Relative frequency compares that with all the trials, so we write it as a fraction.
ASK: Our coin: what was the relative frequency of heads?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: our heads out of 10
trap: writing heads out of tails.
Fix: ask how many tosses there were altogether, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Use the launch data so the word sticks to real results.

beats: MODEL adding the frequencies.
SAY: A spinner was spun and recorded.
First I find the total trials: 9, 6 and 5 make 20.
MODEL writing 9/20, then 0.45 and 45%.
SAY: Red happened 9 times out of 20, so its relative frequency is 9 twentieths.
Times by 5 on top and bottom: 45 hundredths, 0.45, or 45 percent.
ASK: What is the relative frequency of blue, as a percentage?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 30%
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Blue is 6 out of 20, which is 0.3, or 30 percent.
trap: writing 6/14, blue out of the others.
Fix: point to the total, 20, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: What do the three percentages add to? Why?
notes.help: Write 'times it happened' over 'total trials' first.
notes.prep: The anchor in action: times it happened out of the total trials. SC2.

beats: POINT to the tally.
SAY: A dice was rolled 30 times.
Let me check the total first: the frequencies add to 30.
MODEL six.
SAY: Six came up 5 times,
so its relative frequency is 5 out of 30, which simplifies to one sixth.
ASK: What is the relative frequency of rolling a 5?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7/30
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Five came up 7 times out of 30.
That's more than the 5 we'd expect, and that's normal in a small experiment.
trap: writing 7/6 because a dice has 6 faces.
Fix: point to the total rolls, 30, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Which number came up least, and is that a problem?
notes.help: Touch the total before writing the bottom number.
notes.prep: Results vary from the expected chance: sets up Session 3. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: 12 heads in 20 tosses
slides.prompt: What is the relative frequency of heads? Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: puts tails on the bottom instead of the total trials
gives the expected chance, not what actually happened

beats: SAY: A coin was tossed 20 times and landed on heads 12 times.
ASK: What is the relative frequency of heads?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Why isn't it C?
Less -> write times it happened over total trials on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A, 12 out of 20. B divides by tails,
and C is what we expect, not what happened.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: ask what actually happened in these 20 tosses, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. B: wrong denominator; C: expected chance confused with the result.

slides.title: Relative frequency
slides.ask: Write the relative frequency as a fraction and a percentage.
slides.pivot: write times it happened over total trials, then convert
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How did you make the percentage?

items.text: Dice rolled 25 times: six came up 5 times. Six?

items.say: Tails is 50 take away 28, so 22 out of 50: 44 percent.

items.text: Card picked 40 times: red 30 times. Red?

say: Write a fraction and a percentage on your board each time.
trap: using the wrong total on the bottom.
Fix: circle the total trials, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Write each one as a decimal too.
notes.help: Make the bottom number 100 first, then read the percentage.
notes.prep: Guided practice with totals of 10, 25, 50 and 40, and one asked for the other outcome. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Marbles were picked and put back each time.
ASK: What is the relative frequency of yellow, as a percentage?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 20%
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then the coin experiment and Your turn.
Less -> find the total first, 20, then write 4 out of 20. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 4 out of 20 is 20 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 4%.
Fix: ask what the total is, and they make it out of 100.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone with 4% or 4/16 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Run the coin experiment, then work out relative frequencies on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: What is your total number of trials?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: a relative frequency out of the wrong total.
Fix: circle the total trials, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: combining results, two-dice totals and planning an experiment.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: totals of 10 and 100, a fraction frame and hints.
notes.prep: Independent practice: a real experiment, converting forms, reading results and reasoning. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: How often did green come up? Give a fraction, then a percentage.

visual.text: Green came up 9 times in 25 spins.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What is the relative frequency of green, as a fraction and a percentage?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9/25 = 36%
RECORD who uses the wrong total or cannot convert.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing 9/16.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new total, 25, so the percentage needs converting.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you work out a relative frequency.

notes.answer: open - listen for times it happened out of the total trials
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can write a relative frequency three ways?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 9/16 on the board matters most.
ASK: How do you work out a relative frequency?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: times it happened out of the total trials
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: what happens with lots more trials?
